messages:
sara.cs: FYI — ACME reported ~120 users who should have been deprovisioned after an AD group split still have product access. They say they split `ENG-Platform` into `ENG-Platform` + `ENG-Platform-Infra` last night via Azure, and now members from the new infra group still see the old roles in our app. :confused:

aaron.support: Customer provided a timeline: AD split at 23:12 UTC, Azure provisioning ran at 23:20 and 23:35. Our SCIM logs show a group update + a few group deletes. They say they expect immediate removal of role bindings when the source AD group is no longer present.

miguel.eng: Can you paste the SCIM events? curious if Azure sent a "replace" or a "delete + create" pattern. We match by `externalId` on groups — if externalId changed we'll treat it as a new group.

sara.cs: Pasted below from customer and our logs.

scim-bot: [1799001202] scim.event: POST /scim/v2/Groups 201 created externalId=AD-ENG-PLATFORM-2026-1 for group id=g_8f1a
scim-bot: [1799001243] scim.event: PATCH /scim/v2/Groups 200 replace members for group id=g_8f1a
scim-bot: [1799001260] scim.event: POST /scim/v2/Groups 201 created externalId=AD-ENG-PLATFORM-INFRA-2026 for group id=g_d4c2
scim-bot: [1799001270] scim.event: DELETE /scim/v2/Groups?externalId=AD-ENG-PLATFORM-2026-1 404 no match

aaron.support: So we created a new group (g_d4c2) for the infra group, but the old group record (g_8f1a) still has role assignments — and the attempted delete returned 404 by externalId. Customer's Azure looks like it generated new externalId tokens for both new groups rather than updating the original externalId.

lena-idp: Azure's "group rename / split" sometimes does a delete+create with new objectId/externalId. If we only map by externalId, deletes will fail because the old externalId may never be sent by Azure. We should verify we also match by the incoming "meta.resourceType" or altIdentifier if present.

miguel.eng: Quick repro from our test tenant: 1) create group with externalId X 2) Azure split creates new group with externalId Y 3) provisioning sends create(Y) and delete(X) but sometimes the delete uses a different identifier (objectId) => we see 404 and leave bindings on the old internal group. So root cause: delete didn't match our stored externalId -> orphaned role bindings.

sara.cs: Customer asked for immediate remediation: remove role assignment for users who are not in any currently-mapped group for ACME org. They don't want to wait for Azure changes.

miguel.eng: Two options: a) run a one-off cleanup that scans ACME org groups vs latest Azure SCIM manifest and removes role bindings from groups that are gone, or b) support additional matching heuristics for group deletes (match by displayName + members overlap as fallback). Option (a) is faster for the customer.

aaron.support: Can you provide the SQL-ish query and safe delta patch to run? want to get approval from customer before touching.

miguel.eng: Here's a safe approach — compute set difference of user->roles via API, then send targeted PATCHes to remove assignments. Example (pseudo):
```bash
# get all current ACME group externalIds we have
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.com/orgs/acme/scim/Groups
# get latest provisioning dump from Azure (customer provided)
# compute users who are not in any Azure-provided group
# for each user-role to remove, call:
PATCH /admin/orgs/acme/users/{user_id}/roles
payload: {"remove": ["role:platform-engineer"]}
```

miguel.eng: Also attaching the raw SCIM patch we used to remove a role assignment via the internal admin endpoint:
```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "remove",
      "path": "roles[display eq \"platform-engineer\"]"
    }
  ]
}
```

lena-idp: Heads up — customer must confirm they have exported the authoritative group membership list. If Azure is still in flux and does create/delete in subsequent runs, cleanup could reintroduce access or remove the wrong people. We should recommend freezing provisioning for 10–15 minutes or applying an "audit only" run.

sara.cs: I asked ACME to provide the latest provisioning export and to pause automatic provisioning for 30m while we run cleanup. They're ok with that. They also asked if we can add a guard in our code to detect repeated 404 deletes for the same org and surface a warning.

miguel.eng: I'll open a small MR: detect repeated delete failures per org within a 1h window -> create a ticket and surface to the console and slack alert. For immediate support I can run the one-off cleanup if customer signs off.

aaron.support: Customer signed off via email. Action items: @miguel.eng run cleanup job and paste audit log. @lena-idp please review matching heuristics PR to avoid recurrence. @sara.cs confirm audit log with customer after job.

scim-bot: [1799001527] scim.task: scheduled cleanup job started for org=acme initiated_by=miguel.eng
scim-bot: [1799001538] scim.task: cleanup finished. 118 role bindings removed, 2 warnings for accounts not found. Audit: https://internal.redwood/acme/cleanup/1799001527

sara.cs: Sent audit to customer; they confirmed 117/118 expected and one user had a service account that needed special handling. Customer happy, moving to close but flagged us to improve matching to avoid manual steps. :thumbsup:
